51563779.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to His-tagged recombinant IGF2BP1 (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: SPR screening was performed using a Biacore 8k (GE healthcare) instrument at 25 °C. An NTA sensor chip was activated by using sulfo-N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS)/1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethyl aminopropyl) carbodiimide (EDC) chemistry. The compounds were dissolved in DMSO and further diluted with PBS-T buffer and analyzed at a final concentration of 10 μM (5% DMSO). The results were analyzed with the Biacore evaluation software (8k, ver. 2.0). The interaction between CuB and IGF2BP1 was fitted to the steady-state affinity model to obtain results.
original_paragraph.Figure 8 caption: Figure 8. SPR experiments to analyze the binding curves and fitted results of CuB (A) and A11 (B) by immobilizing IGF2BP1 on an NTA sensor chip.
original_paragraph.Figure 8 A: CuB binding with IGF2BP1 Relative response (RU) 0 500 1000 1500 Time (s) K_D = 66.2 nM 0.31 μM 0.625 μM 1.25 μM 2.5 μM 5 μM
original_paragraph.Figure 8 B: A11 binding with IGF2BP1 Relative response (RU) 0 500 1000 1500 Time (s) K_D = 2.88 nM 0.625 μM 1.25 μM 2.5 μM 5 μM 10 μM
original_paragraph.Results Section: Binding Affinity of A11 toward IGF2BP1 by Surface Plasmon Resonance. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free detection technique. SPR-based biosensor assays allow direct measurements of protein–ligand interactions by determining the kinetic parameters and the affinity. It has been reported that the IGF2BP1 KH1–2 domain can covalently bind to CuB with a high affinity and then disrupt the IGF2BP1–m6A interaction. Thus, we performed SPR assay to investigate if compound A11 directly binds to IGF2BP1 and determine its binding affinity. As shown in Table S1 (Supporting Information), A11 displayed a high binding affinity for IGF2BP1 with a K_D value of 2.88 nM, which is superior to that of CuB (K_D = 66.2 nM). In addition, compound A11 was covalently bound to IGF2BP1 in an irreversible manner (Figure 8), which was similar to that of CuB. Meanwhile, microscale thermophoresis (MST) experiments demonstrated that A11 directly bound to IGF2BP1 with a dissociation constant of 10.9 nM (Figure S1).

analyte.concentration_range: 0.31 μM - 5 μM for CuB; 0.625 μM - 10 μM for A11
